mainTopic: Whether משניות and a ברייתא about balconies, cisterns and wall ledges settle the dispute between רב and שמואל over a spot reached by lowering versus throwing.
overview: On the previous amud, רב and שמואל disagree about a spot that one group can reach only by lowering things down (שלשול) and another group only by throwing things up (זריקה). שמואל gives the spot to the lowering side, and רב forbids it to both. The גמרא first tries to prove שמואל from the משנה about a ten-טפחים mound that goes to the מרפסת. רב הונא answers that the משנה means people living right on the balcony, who reach the mound easily. The גמרא then shows that 'לחצר' in the משנה means 'also to the courtyard,' so a shared spot is forbidden to both sides. A second attempt uses the cistern rim and the rock. There the גמרא asks how a cistern can be used without lowering a bucket. אביי answers that it is full of untithed produce (טבל), which is not removed on שבת. The גמרא also explains why the משנה needs both the cistern and the rock. Finally, a ברייתא about courtyard and upper-story residents seems to prove רב, because a middle ledge would be forbidden. רב נחמן answers that the ברייתא speaks of a nineteen-טפחים wall, which has no middle zone at all.

steps.title: The balcony people are really upper-story residents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה's 'מרפסת' refers to בני עלייה, the residents of an upper story. They are called by that name because they go up and down by way of the balcony.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means the upper-story residents. And why do we call them 'balcony'? Because they go up by way of the balcony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains who the משנה means by 'מרפסת': the people who live upstairs and climb up through the balcony. This reading sets up a proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה means upper-story residents, they are above the ten-טפחים mound and can only use it by lowering things down. Meanwhile the חצר residents below could only use it by throwing things up. That turns the משנה's case into exactly the case that רב and שמואל argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: balcony or gallery leading to upper apartments

steps.confusionAlert: The first two words answer a question on the previous amud ('what case are we dealing with?'). Read them as 'It is talking about the upper-story residents.'

phrases.english: [It means] the residents of the upper story.
phrases.notes: This answers the question just asked: who is the משנה talking about?

phrases.english: And why do they call it 'balcony'?
Because they go up by way of the balcony.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the previous amud about whom the משנה means by 'מרפסת'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the משנה, 'מרפסת' means the upper-story residents who use the balcony to go up.

steps.title: So the lowering side wins, which supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: From this reading, the גמרא concludes that a spot used by one side through שלשול and by the other through זריקה is given to the lowering side. That is שמואל's view, and it is difficult for רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see from here: whenever one side reaches a place by lowering and the other by throwing, we give it to the side that lowers!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the משנה: the side that lowers things gets the spot. This seems to prove שמואל right against רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lowering things down is easier than throwing them up, so שמואל gives the spot to the lowering side. רב says both sides are forbidden. The משנה gives the high mound to the 'balcony' group, meaning the upper residents who lower, so it seems to match שמואל exactly.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof held, רב's position would be refuted by a משנה.

phrases.english: We see from here: whenever [a place is used] by this one through lowering
and by that one through throwing,
we give it to the one who uses it by lowering!
phrases.notes: This is שמואל's view, so the משנה seems to be a difficulty for רב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a legal conclusion from the reading in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that a lowering-versus-throwing spot goes to the lowering side (against רב).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה gives the ten-טפחים mound to the 'מרפסת', read as the upper-story residents.

steps.title: No, the משנה means people living on the balcony itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא uses רב הונא's reading from another place: the משנה means people whose homes open directly onto the balcony. They reach the mound on their own level, so this is not a lowering-versus-throwing case.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב הונא said, 'to those who live on the balcony.' Here too, it means those who live on the balcony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. It explains the משנה differently, so the משנה no longer speaks about רב and שמואל's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The balcony residents stand at the height of the ten-טפחים mound, so they can use it easily without lowering anything. The חצר residents would have to throw things up. Easy use against hard use gives the spot to the balcony, and רב can agree to that.

phrases.english: As Rav Huna said
'to those who live on the balcony.'
phrases.notes: רב הונא said this about a later משנה.

phrases.english: Here too,
[it means] those who live on the balcony.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 2 by redefining who the משנה means.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading that 'מרפסת' means upper-story residents.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה may refer to people living on the balcony level, who need no lowering, so it says nothing about the lowering-versus-throwing case.

steps.title: Then why does a low mound go only to the courtyard?
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה means balcony-level residents, the סיפא is hard to explain. A mound lower than ten טפחים is easy for both sides to reach, like two groups that each have their own doorway. Why should it belong only to the חצר?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the last clause: 'less than this — to the courtyard.' Why? It is like 'this one by a doorway and that one by a doorway'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading from the end of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With balcony-level residents, a low mound is easy for the balcony people to step down to and easy for the חצר people to reach. When both sides have equally easy access, neither should win. So giving it to the חצר alone looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: each side has its own doorway, meaning equal easy access

phrases.english: If so, read the last clause:
Less than this, [it belongs] to the courtyard.
Why?
It is [a case of] one side by a doorway and the other side by a doorway!
phrases.notes: Equal access for both sides, so neither should get the spot alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading in step 3 using the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'מרפסת' means balcony-level residents.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading, a low mound is equally easy for both sides, so the סיפא should not give it to the חצר alone.

steps.title: 'To the courtyard' means 'also to the courtyard,' so both are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'לחצר' means 'also to the courtyard.' The חצר residents can use the spot too, so both sides share it, and without an עירוב both are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'to the courtyard' mean? Also to the courtyard. And both of them are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the משנה's words differently. The low mound is not given to the חצר alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only means that the חצר also has a claim, not that it has the only claim. Since both sides have equal access and made no עירוב together, both are forbidden to carry there. This fits רב הונא's reading, and the משנה no longer proves שמואל against רב.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה does not prove שמואל. The high mound goes to people living on the balcony because they reach it easily. The low mound is shared, so both sides are forbidden without an עירוב.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'לחצר' as 'only to the courtyard.' The גמרא reads it as 'also to the courtyard,' which leads to both sides being forbidden.

phrases.english: What does 'to the courtyard' mean?
Also to the courtyard.
And both of them are forbidden.
phrases.notes: Both sides have equal access and no עירוב between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לחצר' seemed to give the low mound only to the חצר.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לחצר' means 'also to the courtyard,' so both sides share access and both are forbidden.

steps.title: Support from the later clause of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says its reading of 'לחצר' as 'also to the courtyard' makes sense, and quotes the סיפא about a mound that is far from the balcony.
steps.simpleTranslation: This reading also makes sense, because the end of the משנה teaches: When is this said? When the mound is close to the balcony. But if it is far away, even if it is ten טפחים high, it goes 'to the courtyard.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the answer it just gave, 'לחצר' means 'also to the courtyard.' Here it only quotes the end of the משנה. The argument itself comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא uses the same word 'לחצר' about a mound that is far from the balcony. If that clause can only make sense as 'also to the courtyard,' then the earlier 'לחצר' can be read the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical. Introduces support for the previous answer.
Close by. The mound is near the balcony.
Distant. The mound is set apart from the balcony.

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
since the latter clause teaches:
In what case is this said? When it is near.
phrases.notes: 'It' means the mound or embankment, close to the balcony.

phrases.english: But when it is distant,
even if it is ten handbreadths high, it is 'to the courtyard.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the תירוץ of step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The reading 'לחצר' means 'also to the courtyard.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה about a distant mound.

steps.title: The plain meaning of 'to the courtyard' does not fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'לחצר' means in the סיפא. It rules out the simple reading that the courtyard alone may use it, because the spot belongs to both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'to the courtyard' mean? If you say it belongs to the courtyard and they may carry there, why should that be? It is the domain of both of them!
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the proof, the גמרא shows that the simple meaning of 'לחצר' in the סיפא cannot be right. This clears the way for its own reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the mound is far from the balcony, neither side has easier access. So the courtyard has no reason to get it alone. That means 'לחצר' cannot mean 'only to the courtyard.'

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. Introduces a reading that will be rejected.
The domain of both of them

phrases.english: What does 'to the courtyard' mean?
If you say: to the courtyard, and it is permitted to them,
why? It is the domain of both of them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the סיפא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'לחצר' in the סיפא as 'only to the courtyard, permitted.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A far-off mound is equally reachable by both sides, so it cannot belong to the courtyard alone.

steps.title: In the later clause, 'to the courtyard' means also to the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: So 'לחצר' in the סיפא must mean 'also to the courtyard,' and without an עירוב both sides are forbidden to carry there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'to the courtyard' mean? Also to the courtyard, and both are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the only reading of the סיפא that works: the spot is shared, so both sides are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the spot is shared, neither group can carry there without an עירוב. This proves the משנה itself uses 'לחצר' to mean 'also to the courtyard.'

keyTerms.meaning: Both are forbidden to carry there

phrases.english: Rather, what does 'to the courtyard' mean?
Also to the courtyard, and both are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לחצר' means the courtyard alone may use it.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לחצר' means also the courtyard, so it is shared and forbidden to both.

steps.title: The same meaning applies to the earlier clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies the same meaning to the earlier 'לחצר' and concludes: שמע מינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, what does 'to the courtyard' mean? Also to the courtyard, and both are forbidden. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא carries the meaning from the סיפא back to the earlier clause and declares the proof complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word in the same משנה should mean the same thing. So the answer in step 5 is confirmed, and רב הונא's reading of the משנה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this. A formula of conclusion.

steps.whatToRemember: In this משנה, 'לחצר' means 'also to the courtyard.' The spot is shared, so without an עירוב both sides are forbidden to carry there. This keeps the משנה from being a proof against רב.

phrases.english: Here too: what does 'to the courtyard' mean?
Also to the courtyard, and both are forbidden.
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the result of step 8 to the earlier clause.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'לחצר' means 'also to the courtyard' throughout the משנה. So רב's position survives.

steps.title: A new attempted proof from the cistern rim and the rock
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another משנה: a cistern rim or rock ten טפחים high goes to the balcony, and a lower one goes to the courtyard. This again seems to favor the lowering side, like שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: The rim of a cistern and a rock that are ten טפחים high go to the balcony. If lower than that, they go to the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attempt to prove שמואל right and רב wrong, using a different משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'balcony' means the upper-floor residents, they would use a tall rim or rock by lowering things down onto it. The courtyard residents would have to throw things up onto it. Giving it to the balcony would then mean the lowering side wins, which is שמואל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The raised rim around a cistern

phrases.english: We learned: The rim of a cistern and the rock
that are ten handbreadths high go to the balcony;
lower than this, they go to the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was turned aside, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל: lowering beats throwing (and this is difficult for רב).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a cistern rim and a rock

steps.title: רב הונא: it means people living on the balcony level
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that 'balcony' here means people whose homes open onto the balcony. So no lowering is involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: It means those who live on the balcony.
steps.whatsHappening: The proof for שמואל is pushed aside with the same answer used before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The balcony-level residents reach a ten-טפחים rock at their own height, without lowering anything. So the case is not lowering against throwing, and it proves nothing against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who live on the balcony, whose homes open onto it

phrases.english: רב הונא said:
To those who live on the balcony.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לְאוֹתָן הַדָּרִים בַּמִּרְפֶּסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 10 using the reading from step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely by redefining who 'balcony' refers to.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof wrongly assumed 'balcony' means upper-story residents who lower things.

steps.title: That works for a rock, but what about a cistern?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא: a rock's top can be used at balcony level, but a cistern's water lies below and can only be reached by lowering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine for a rock. But for a cistern, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's answer. It fits the rock, but not the cistern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To draw water from a cistern you must lower a bucket down to it. So even balcony-level residents use it by lowering. The 'lowering' problem comes back, and it is unclear why the cistern should go to the balcony.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine; granted. It admits one case works in order to challenge another.
What is there to say? A challenge.

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the cistern's rim, which sits at a usable height. It is about the water inside, which can only be reached by lowering a bucket.

phrases.english: This works well for a rock.
For a cistern, what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח סֶלַע. בּוֹר מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's reading from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's reading that 'balcony' means balcony-level residents
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A cistern is used by lowering a bucket even from balcony level, so the reading does not remove the lowering issue.

steps.title: A cistern full of water
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה answers that the משנה speaks of a cistern filled to the top with water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק, the son of רב יהודה, said: Here we are dealing with a cistern that is full of water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 12. If the cistern is full, the water is near the top, so the balcony people can reach it without lowering anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that a cistern's water is usually deep below balcony level. רב יצחק removes that problem by picturing a full cistern, so the water sits right at the top. That keeps רב הונא's reading alive: balcony residents use it directly, and no lowering is involved.

keyTerms.meaning: A cistern, a pit that stores water
We are dealing with (this is the case under discussion)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak, son of Rav Yehuda, said:
Here we are dealing with a cistern full of water.
phrases.notes: Full means the water is up near the balcony, so it can be reached without lowering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A cistern's water is deep, so using it requires lowering.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cistern is full, so the water is reachable from balcony level.

steps.title: But the water level goes down
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a full cistern does not stay full once people draw from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it becomes less full!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just heard. Once people start drawing water, the level drops, and soon they will have to lower a bucket after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being full is only a temporary state. As the water is used, it sinks below balcony level. So the lowering problem comes back, and the answer from step 13 does not hold up for long.

keyTerms.meaning: It becomes lacking; it goes down

phrases.english: But it diminishes!
phrases.notes: Drawing water lowers the level, so lowering a bucket will eventually be needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a full cistern avoids lowering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full cistern empties as it is used, so lowering becomes necessary again.

steps.title: Allowed when full, so allowed when low
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that since using the cistern was allowed while it was full, that permission continues even after the level drops.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is allowed when it is full, it is also allowed when it is lacking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to defend the full-cistern answer. It argues that the cistern's starting status, permitted, carries over even after the water goes down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the הלכה follows the cistern's starting condition. Since the cistern began in a permitted state, it should stay permitted. If so, the falling water level does not change anything.

phrases.english: Since when it is full it is permitted —
when it is lacking it is also permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Carrying the permitted status over from the full state
steps.terutzHavaAmina: When the level drops, the cistern becomes forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permission it had when full continues when it is low.

steps.title: The opposite argument works just as well
steps.stepSummary: With אדרבה, the גמרא flips the reasoning: since using the cistern is forbidden when it is low, it should be forbidden even when full.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Since it is forbidden when it is lacking, it should also be forbidden when it is full.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reasoning of step 15 by turning it upside down. Nothing proves which state should decide the other, so the full-cistern answer falls apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 let the full state control the low state. You could just as easily let the low state control the full state. Since the argument works equally well in both directions, it proves nothing, and רב יצחק's answer is dropped.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the reverse is more logical

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as a final ruling that a full cistern is forbidden. The אדרבה only shows that step 15's argument cuts both ways, so it cannot be relied on.

phrases.english: On the contrary,
since when it is lacking it is forbidden —
when it is full it should also be forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 15 by reversing its logic.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the carry-over argument, and with it רב יצחק's full-water explanation.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The reasoning can be reversed just as easily, so it proves nothing.

steps.title: A cistern full of produce
steps.stepSummary: אביי offers a new answer: the cistern is filled with produce, not water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: Here we are dealing with a cistern full of produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The full-water answer failed, so the גמרא brings a new answer from אביי. The cistern is used to store produce piled up to the top, which balcony residents can reach directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא tells us the previous answer is being thrown out. Like water, produce at the top is near balcony level, so nothing needs to be lowered. This keeps רב הונא's reading alive in a new way.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
Here we are dealing with a cistern full of produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 13 with a new case setup.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Water in a cistern requires lowering.
steps.terutzMaskana: Produce stored up to the top is reachable from balcony level.

steps.title: But the produce also goes down
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that produce also shrinks as people take from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they become less!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the same problem as before. As people take produce, the pile shrinks, and soon they will need to reach down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same attack as in step 14, now aimed at אביי's answer. A pile of produce gets smaller just like a pool of water does.

keyTerms.meaning: They diminish (plural, referring to the produce)

phrases.english: But they diminish!
phrases.notes: Same objection as step 14, now about produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer in step 17.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Produce is used up, so the pile drops below balcony level.

steps.title: The produce is untithed, so none is taken
steps.stepSummary: The produce is טבל (untithed). It cannot be eaten or tithed on שבת, so it is never removed, and the level stays at the top.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about טבל, untithed produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the gap in אביי's answer. Because the produce is טבל, nobody may take any of it on שבת, so the pile stays at balcony level all day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You may not separate tithes on שבת, and you may not eat טבל. So the produce will not be used on שבת, and the pile will not shrink. The problem of the falling level is gone, and אביי's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: טבל: produce from which the required tithes have not yet been separated

steps.whatToRemember: To defend רב הונא, the cistern must stay full all of שבת. Water fails because it gets used up. Untithed produce works, because it cannot be touched on שבת, so its level never drops.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רב הונא's reading, so the cistern case no longer proves the view that favors lowering. It also shows how a separate law, not tithing on שבת, can lock a case into place.

phrases.english: With untithed produce.
phrases.notes: Tithes may not be separated on שבת, so this produce stays untouched and the pile stays high.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 18 and completes אביי's answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The produce will be used up and the level will drop.
steps.terutzMaskana: Untithed produce cannot be used on שבת, so the level stays constant.

steps.title: The wording of the משנה supports this reading
steps.stepSummary: The cistern is listed together with the rock, so, like the rock, the cistern case is about using its surface. The גמרא accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise, because it teaches the cistern together with the rock. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a support from the wording of the משנה for the answer it just gave. It then accepts that answer as correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a rock, people only use the top surface. The משנה lists the cistern in the same breath, which suggests the cistern case is also about using its top, not about drawing from what is inside. This backs up the idea that the cistern is full of produce that stays at the top level.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise; the text itself supports this reading.
Learn from this; the point is proven.

phrases.english: It is also precise (from the wording)
since it teaches it together with a rock.
phrases.notes: A rock is only used on its surface, so the cistern case is about its surface too.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer from Step 19 using the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The explanation that the cistern case is about using its full surface (produce that is never removed).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה lists the cistern next to the rock.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need both cases?
steps.stepSummary: If the cistern and the rock work the same way, why mention both?
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do I need it to teach a cistern, and why do I need it to teach a rock?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the cistern and the rock now seem identical, the גמרא asks why the משנה bothered to list both. This sets up an explanation of what each case adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that a משנה does not repeat itself for no reason. If both cases teach the same rule, one of them looks extra. The גמרא wants to know what each one adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asking why something seems extra)
A cistern; a pit for holding water or storage.

phrases.english: And why do I need it to teach a cistern
and why do I need it to teach a rock?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמָה לִי לְמִיתְנֵא בּוֹר וּלְמָה לִי לְמִיתְנֵא סֶלַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once the cistern and rock are shown to be parallel, the גמרא asks why both are needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the משנה, which lists both a cistern and a rock.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two cases teach the same rule, one of them seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Both cases are needed
steps.stepSummary: A rock alone would not teach us about a cistern. A cistern could sometimes hold permitted produce that gets removed, so we might have thought the רבנן would make a גזירה against using it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If it had taught us only a rock, we would say that is because there is no reason to make a decree. But a cistern, we might decree against, because sometimes it is filled with tithed produce. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both cases are needed. The rock alone would not tell us that a cistern is also allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rock never shrinks, so there is no worry at all. A cistern full of produce could sometimes hold tithed produce (פירות מתוקנין), which people may take out and eat on שבת. That would lower the level, so we might have expected a גזירה against using cisterns in general. Listing the cistern teaches that no such decree was made.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary; both cases are needed.
To make a rabbinic decree (גזירה) as a safeguard.
Produce that has already been tithed and may be eaten.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of produce. In the case we rely on, the produce is טבל (untithed), which cannot be eaten on שבת, so it stays put. The worry here is a different cistern filled with tithed produce, which people could take out.

phrases.english: It is necessary (to teach both),
for if it had taught us only a rock —
(we would say that is because) there is nothing to decree against,
but a cistern — let us decree (against using it),
since sometimes it is filled with tithed produce,
phrases.notes: Tithed produce can be removed and eaten, which would lower the level.

phrases.english: (therefore) it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case teaches something the other could not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought the cistern is forbidden because of a גזירה, in case it is filled with tithed produce that gets removed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cistern case teaches that no such decree was made, so it may be used like a rock.

steps.title: A ברייתא about courtyard and upper-story residents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the רב and שמואל dispute and quotes a ברייתא: if they forgot to make an עירוב, courtyard residents use the lower ten טפחים and upper-story residents use the upper ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If the courtyard residents and the upper-story residents forgot and did not make an עירוב, the courtyard residents use the lower ten handbreadths and the upper-story residents use the upper ten. How so? If a ledge sticks out of the wall below ten, it belongs to the courtyard. If it is above ten, it belongs to the upper story.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the dispute between רב and שמואל and brings a ברייתא as a possible proof. This step lays out the source. The actual inference comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute is about a space that one group can reach easily (by lowering things) and the other group can reach only with effort (by throwing). רב says it is forbidden to both groups; שמואל gives it to the group that reaches it easily. The ברייתא divides the wall: the bottom ten טפחים go to the courtyard and the top ten go to the upper story.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source brought as proof).
The upper story; an upstairs apartment.
They made an עירוב, joining their properties so they may carry on שבת.
A ledge that sticks out from a wall.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The residents of a courtyard and the residents of an upper story
who forgot and did not make an eiruv —
the courtyard residents use the lower ten (handbreadths),
and the upper-story residents use the upper ten.
How so?
A ledge sticking out from the wall:
below ten — it belongs to the courtyard;
above ten — it belongs to the upper story.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the cistern discussion and returns to the main dispute between רב and שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that a space reachable by one group easily and the other with effort is forbidden to both.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about courtyard and upper-story residents who did not make an עירוב.

steps.title: The middle zone is forbidden to both
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא, the גמרא infers that a ledge in the zone between the lower ten and the upper ten is forbidden to everyone. This matches רב and challenges שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that a ledge in between is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the key inference from the ברייתא: the in-between area belongs to neither group, so it is forbidden. This seems to prove רב right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives only the bottom ten טפחים to the courtyard and only the top ten to the upper story. A ledge in the middle can be reached by both groups, one easily and one with effort. If it is forbidden, that fits רב, who forbids it to both. שמואל would have given it to the group that reaches it easily.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a direct attempt to settle the dispute between רב and שמואל with a ברייתא. It also puts pressure on שמואל to explain this source.

phrases.english: This implies that what is in between is forbidden!
phrases.notes: This fits רב (forbidden to both) and goes against שמואל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא quoted in Step 23.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that the shared middle space is forbidden to both groups.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא assigns only the lower ten and upper ten, implying the middle zone is forbidden.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about a nineteen-handbreadth wall, so it has no middle zone
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rejects the proof from the ברייתא. He sets it in a wall of nineteen טפחים, where there is no middle zone. A ledge below ten belongs to the courtyard residents, who reach it directly, and the upper-story residents can reach it only by lowering things. A ledge above ten belongs to the upper residents, who reach it directly, and the courtyard residents can reach it only by throwing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Here we are dealing with a wall of nineteen טפחים with a ledge sticking out of it. If the ledge is below ten, the courtyard people reach it like walking through a doorway, and the upper people can only reach it by lowering things down. If it is above ten, the upper people reach it like a doorway, and the courtyard people can only reach it by throwing things up.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן is knocking down the proof from Step 24. He says the ברייתא is describing a short wall that has no 'in-between' area, so you cannot learn from it that a middle ledge is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a nineteen-טפחים wall, the bottom ten and the top ten overlap, so every spot is inside one zone or the other. The ברייתא was only explaining which group has easy access and which group has awkward access. Since no forbidden middle zone exists in this case, the inference that matched רב falls away, and שמואל is no longer challenged by it.

keyTerms.meaning: We are dealing with. This formula sets the case in a specific situation.
Doorway or entrance. Here it means easy, direct access, as if walking right in.
Throwing things up to a higher spot

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב נחמן is giving a new ruling on the dispute. He is only saying the ברייתא is about a case with no middle zone, so it cannot be used as proof for either side.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא tool. A proof is defused by placing the source in a specific physical case where the key detail, here the middle zone, simply does not exist.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Here we are dealing with a wall of nineteen [handbreadths],
phrases.notes: Nineteen is less than twenty, so the lower ten and the upper ten overlap. There is no gap between them.

phrases.english: and a ledge protrudes from it.
[If the ledge is] below ten —
for this one [the courtyard residents], it is like an entrance,
phrases.notes: They can reach it easily and directly.

phrases.english: and for that one [the upper residents], only by lowering.
[If the ledge is] above ten —
for this one [the upper residents], it is like an entrance,
and for that one [the courtyard residents], only by throwing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הָכָא בְּכוֹתֶל תִּשְׁעָה עָשָׂר עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference in Step 24 that the ברייתא implies a forbidden middle zone, which had supported רב against שמואל.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the specific inference about a middle-zone ledge. It does not decide the dispute between רב and שמואל itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference assumed the ברייתא's wall has a gap between the lower ten and the upper ten. On a nineteen-טפחים wall, the zones overlap, so no such gap exists.
